title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing + padding-minimizer heuristics (v25)
author: Asha Patel
ci_status: pass (all checks green after one flaky kernel-test rerun)
description:
Motivation:
We continue to see wasted GPU cycles due to padding when batching requests with heterogeneous sequence lengths. This PR iterates on the dynamic-batching seqlen heuristics: it introduces an explicit bucketing step followed by a light-weight padding-minimizer that trades a small scheduling overhead for significant token savings. The heuristics are kernel-aware and scheduling-aware: they expose hints to the scheduler to prefer groupings that match optimized kernel tiling sizes and to avoid forcing KV cache evictions for long-lived contexts.

What this PR does (single-run summary):
- Add a new seqlen bucketing stage in the batch builder that groups incoming requests into configurable bucketing bins (powers-of-two and custom boundaries via config).
- Implement a padding-minimizer that, within each bucket, considers a small combinatorial reordering (bounded by max_explore=3) to minimize total padded tokens while respecting latency SLOs.
- Surface kernel-friendly hints from the batch builder to the scheduler (preferred_tile and prefer_cuda_kernel flags) so the runtime can select the best fused attention kernel for the dominant seq length in the batch.
- Improve KV cache policy: when reordering requests for padding savings, preserve per-request KV affinity where beneficial; avoid evicting hot KV segments by preferring batches that keep long-context requests together.
- Add a bounded continuous-batching delay heuristic: if a short wait (~1-3ms, configurable) can merge a tail request into a near-compatible bucket with net token savings, we do it; otherwise we flush to meet latency SLOs.
- Expose runtime config knobs (seqlen_buckets, max_explore, tail_wait_ms, kernel_hinting=true) and default them to conservative values used in our perf lab.

Benchmarks & results (summary):
- Throughput improvement: +9-15% token/s on mixed short/long workload compared to v24 heuristics in the perf-canary harness (p95 latency unchanged within SLA).
- Cost reduction: ~7% GPU token-cost reduction for a representative customer trace with 60% short (<64) and 40% long (>512) requests.
- Worst-case added scheduling overhead: median +0.6ms in batch-build CPU time for the combinatorial explore; still dominated by kernel execution time so overall latency impact is negligible for our target workloads.

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/batching/batch_builder.cc: add bucketing stage and padding minimizer algorithm (bounded exploration).
- runtime/batching/batch_builder.h: public config knobs and new metrics.
- runtime/scheduler/scheduler.cc: accept kernel hints and prefer tile-aligned scheduling.
- runtime/kv/kv_policy.cc: preserve KV affinity during reorders and add metrics for KV-eviction pressure.
- runtime/config/defaults.yaml: new seqlen_buckets & defaults.
- perf/benchmarks/dynamic_batching_canary.py: new benchmark scenarios and CI harness update.
- tests/batching/test_bucketing.cpp: unit tests for bucketing + padding-minimizer.
- tests/kv/test_kv_affinity.cpp: regressions for eviction behavior.
- docs/runtime/dynamic_batching.md: describe knobs and recommended values.

Testing done:
- Unit tests added and existing batching tests updated.
- Integration perf-canary run on RTX A6000 and NVIDIA H100 org-perf cluster.
- Manual validation with two customer traces (internal redacted).
- Backward compatibility: heuristics default to previous behavior when seqlen_buckets is empty or kernel_hinting=false.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Feature guarded behind runtime flag seqlen_heuristics.v25 (default ON for canary clusters).
- Canary rollout across two regions for 72h with traffic split and rollback script in release helpers.
- Observability: new metrics (batch_padding_tokens_saved, kv_eviction_pressure, batch_builder_time_ms) added to Console dashboards.

Checklist:
- [x] Design reviewed and perf benchmarks attached (perf-canary).
- [x] Unit & integration tests.
- [x] Docs updated with config knobs and recommended settings.
- [x] Canary rollout plan included.

Notes:
- This change is a conservative iteration on prior v24/v23 heuristics; further work (v26) will explore adaptive bucket boundary tuning based on live traffic histograms.
